definitions.explanation: A warm, reddish-brown color resembling polished copper. Used to describe skin tanned by the sun, metallic surfaces, or autumn foliage.

examples.japanese: {銅色|あかがねいろ}に{焼|や}けた{肌|はだ}。
examples.english: Skin tanned to a copper color.

examples.japanese: {夕日|ゆうひ}に{照|て}らされて{屋根|やね}が{銅色|あかがねいろ}に{輝|かがや}いた。
examples.english: Lit by the setting sun, the roof shone with a copper glow.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}で{過|す}ごした{夏|なつ}の{終|お}わりには、{子|こ}どもたちの{肌|はだ}は{銅色|あかがねいろ}になっていた。
examples.english: By the end of a summer spent at the beach, the children's skin had turned a bronze color.

notes: {銅|あかがね} is a classical Japanese word for copper (literally "red metal"), in contrast to the more common modern reading {銅|どう}. The compound {銅色|あかがねいろ} has a literary and evocative quality. It is often used to describe well-tanned skin ({銅色|あかがねいろ}の{肌|はだ}) and conveys a warm, healthy, outdoorsy image. The more colloquial equivalent would be {銅色|どういろ}, though あかがねいろ is preferred in literary or descriptive writing.
